title: overnight-sre-journal-maya-2026-03-20
content:
Quick notes from the overnight shift (handed off at 07:30). Mostly follow-ups + runbook TODOs. Informal scratchpad — clean up later for ops paper.

SUMMARY
- Night had two distinct pages that were related: short-lived 503 spike across hosted-api (23:40–00:10) and repeated autoscaler flaps for dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (01:50–02:30).
- Root cause hypotheses: peer KV-cache eviction storms during heavier-than-expected prefix caching + a delayed autoscaler probe bounce after instance replacement.
- No customer data exposure. No sustained SLO breach; brief latency SLO misses recorded (metric window 5m).

TIMELINE (local times)
- 23:34 alert: host-api-503-rate high (paging rule: >100/min errors) — alert routed to eng-sre.
- 23:36 paged: initial ack by me (Maya). Quick triage, saw 503s from approx 3 frontends; traced to a single host pool where KV cache miss rate spiked.
- 23:40 mitigated by rolling restart of pool-worker-17 (short-term manual mitigation) — errors subsided.
- 00:15 alerted again: autoscaler activity for dedicated-gpu-pool-3 flapping (scale-down then immediate scale-up attempts).
- 01:50 repeated flaps; I left notes in Slack thread and escalated to Samir for deeper infra trace.
- 02:10 found repeated k8s liveness probe failures on nodes with driver 535.21 (weird mismatch with runtime driver 535.23) — likely node replacement timing issue causing transient capacity shortages.
- 03:05 worked with Lena to drain and cordon two suspect nodes; flaps stopped after 03:20.
- 06:45 final check: dashboards green, no further alerts. Handed off to day SRE.

INCIDENT FOLLOW-UPS (action items to close incidents)
- I-2871 (503-spike-hosted-api): Add a short blameless writeup. Who: Maya. Due: 2026-03-22.
  - Attach traces (see linked Slack thread) and correlating KV cache miss graphs.
  - Hypothesis: cache eviction cascade from prefix cache TTL misconfiguration when sequence length distribution skewed. Need to verify prefix hit rates by model and request size.
- I-2872 (autoscaler-flap-dedicated-gpu-pool-3): Postmortem draft + repro steps. Who: Samir + Maya. Due: 2026-03-25.
  - Capture node replacement timings, k8s probe latencies, and driver versions.
  - Check cloud provider instance replacement logs (possible instance image drift).

RUNBOOK / INFRA TODOS (short actionable tasks)
- Runbook: add step for "kv-cache storm" in hosted-api runbook (priority medium).
  - Short description, quick mitigation (isolate pool, force cache warm, scale temporary frontends), and observability checks.
- Runbook: add autoscaler probe hysteresis recommendation for GPU pools (longer grace, backoff on consecutive flaps).
- Infra: create automated job to detect driver version drift across nodes in a pool and alert if mismatch >1 patch. Owner: Lena. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Metric: add a composite metric that correlates "prefix-KV-miss-rate" with "503 error rate" and alert on correlation > threshold. Owner: Maya. ETA: 1 week.

NOTES TO SELF / SHORTHAND
- When chasing KV issues: check prefix cache hit heatmap first (grafana -> hosted-api -> cache -> prefix-hit-heatmap). Saves time.
- If autoscaler flaps: look at kube events for scaleDown/scaleUp cycles; probe failures are often the silent trigger.
- Use `kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp` on suspected nodes for timeline.
- Remember to include sequence-length histogram in any follow-up (we saw longer-than-usual sequences at 23:30-23:45).

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS
- Why did pool-worker-17 show the highest miss rate? Was it a cold restart or an OOM kill earlier? Check pod-level OOM/kubelet logs.
- Where did the driver patch drift come from? Image build or provider rolling update? Need infra team's build logs.

SLACK/TRACES/PR LINKS (for PM/Infra)
- Slack thread (primary): https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C03ABCD123/p1700400000000
- Traces grouped: trace ids in Slack thread (see thread for list) — attach to I-2871.
- Infra PR placeholder (autoscaler hysteresis): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812 (WIP, Samir assigned).

QUICK TODOS (today morning handoff)
- [ ] Draft I-2871 short blameless note (Maya) — send to eng-sre for review.
- [ ] Add runbook bullet for kv-cache storm (Maya).
- [ ] Start a short infra ticket for driver-drift detection (Lena) — reference in I-2872.
- [ ] Pair with Samir to capture node replacement logs for I-2872 (Samir + Maya) — schedule 2026-03-21 10:00.

MISC
- Paging noise: consider tweaking the hosted-api 503 alert to a 1.5x baseline during midnight UTC window when traffic is anomalous for the model eval jobs (but defer to product if that would hide real regressions).
- Small ops note: heartbeat probe timeout for GPU pools currently 5s — candidate for increase to 8s plus a single retry.

END OF SCRATCHPAD — will tidy into formal incident pages and runbook edits later.
